turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. It’s very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably just me being a bit silly, but... well, I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

I don't want you to think I keep a messy house—I really do try my best to keep things nice—but right now, my kitchen table is just completely covered. It's got all my husband’s medical appointment papers, and flyers from church, and little notes from the senior center, plus all these half-finished to-do lists I keep making. I just sit there looking at it all, and I honestly don't know which thing I'm supposed to do first. And then, before I know it, the whole day is just gone and I haven't done any of it. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have similar difficulties with focus, organization, or completing tasks when you were a child?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose I did. I always wanted to be a good student, I really did, but... well, my mother kept all my old report cards, and I'm a little embarrassed to say it, but the teachers usually wrote that I was a bright little girl, but... careless. That was the word they always used. 

I didn't mean to be, of course! But I was just always forgetting my books, or leaving my homework behind. And, um, they constantly had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside to play. I'd just sit there and get so lost in my own little world instead of finishing my papers. 

Is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I hope I don't sound like I was a terrible child, Doctor, I really did try my best to be good and do what I was told.
